posts.text:
JOB OFFER: Looking for a voice.

Details below 😉

We’ll take your voice, your face, your likeness. We’ll clone them, reuse them and make them available whenever needed.

Sounds uncomfortable when written like that, doesn’t it?

This is not theoretical. I’ve personally received offers of up to €10,000 to sell my voice or the voice of someone on my team.

We’ve always sold our work, our time and our performances. But now we’re increasingly being asked to sell parts of ourselves and personally, I’m against that.

I don’t believe our voice, our face or our identity should simply become assets with a price tag. Maybe we’ve started to forget that not everything about us should be for sale.

Little by little, we’re giving more and more of ourselves to large companies: our voices, our faces, our identities, our data and at some point, I think we have to ask where the line is.

When are we no longer selling a service, but selling ourselves in pieces? WAKE UP! 

Would you accept this job offer?

Disney is going vertical and this could change much more than the way we watch stories! Why?

We’ve spent the last few years helping vertical stories find their Italian voices and seeing Disney explore this space feels like another sign that vertical storytelling is becoming something much bigger.

Disney+ has already introduced Verts, its vertical video experience for mobile, experimented with vertical-first short-form storytelling through Locker Diaries and explored microdrama opportunities with DramaBox. More recently, Disney and TikTok also announced a partnership that will bring curated short-form content into Disney+.

As the format grows and travels across markets, giving these stories an authentic local voice will become part of the challenge too.

We’ve spent the last few years doing exactly that for Italian audiences.

So Disney Entertainment, whenever Italy becomes part of this journey, we’d love to talk ✨

What are you actually paying for when you hire a dubbing studio for your vertical drama?

You’re paying for someone to choose the right actors, assign the right characters, adapt the dialogue, coordinate recordings, catch mistakes, manage retakes, check consistency, edit, mix, master and deliver the final version synced back to picture with the M&E.

Sometimes we’re asked to provide voices only and we’re happy to do that too.

But when we manage the full workflow, what the client is really paying for is something much simpler: not having to worry about every single step themselves.

The whole workflow stays within our Italian team, with nothing outsourced outside the process. That continuity is also part of what the production fee covers: one team, one workflow and one responsibility from start to finish.

Your vertical drama isn’t getting the views you expected. Who’s mixing it… and do they actually speak Italian? We’ve seen projects where syllables were cut, takes were joined incorrectly or pitch effects made dramatic performances sound almost cartoon-like and in a market like Italy, where dubbing plays such an important role, that can directly affect whether viewers stay engaged or simply swipe away.

That’s why our workflow stays native Italian from recording to final mix: voice actors, dialogue adapters, QC, audio post-production, management and more. 

If you’re planning your next Italian vertical drama, let’s talk. Email, videocall or phone, whatever is easier for you.

At the beginning, we were simply a group of professionals trying to do our best. Then, almost without noticing, that group became a team.

New voice actors joined us. New ways of organizing our work. We made mistakes, found solutions, refined our workflow, learned to trust one another and built processes that now feel second nature but simply didn’t exist 130 dramas ago.

It’s funny. When you’re looking ahead, it always feels like there’s still a long road in front of you.

Today, our team has surpassed 130 dubbed vertical dramas across platforms including CandyJar, DramaWave, DramaBox, ShortMax and JoyReel.

The number itself is just a consequence.

What truly makes me proud is everything that happened while that number was growing: the people who became part of this journey, the trust we built one project at a time. 

If project number 131 teaches us even one new lesson, then we’ll know we’re still moving in the right direction.
